takes.prompt: Genre: dark orchestral video game soundtrack, eerie folklore, in the spirit of Ori and the Blind Forest's darker cues. BPM: 76. Key: D minor. Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. Setting: Pine Hollow at night - lanterns glowing between black pines, fog on the ground, an ancient guardian stirring in the old-growth; hushed and unsettling, never scary. Arrangement: a lonely alto flute and solo viola melody over sul tasto string harmonics and a slow harp ostinato; pizzicato basses and cellos walk underneath, and a soft, steady pulse of frame drum, low toms and muffled timpani runs under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: dark concert-hall reverb.

Genre: epic orchestral video game boss battle music, dark folklore. BPM: 120. Key: D minor. Instrumental only, no vocals, no choir. The fight with the Antler King, an ancient forest guardian gone wrong, in a fog-filled clearing of standing stones and hanging lanterns - relentless, ominous, heroic underneath. Arrangement: driving spiccato string ostinatos, a menacing French horn and low brass theme, cello and double-bass runs; a powerful, steady groove of taiko, timpani, bass drum and toms runs under the whole piece from the second bar to the end. No fade-out: the last bar is as full as the rest. Production: big concert-hall sound.

Genre: warm orchestral video game victory and dawn theme in the spirit of Joe Hisaishi. BPM: 84. Key: D major. Instrumental only, no vocals, no lead choir. The quest's end: the Antler King is laid to rest and the first light of dawn rises over Pine Hollow, the fog lifting from the pines - relief, warmth, quiet triumph. Arrangement: a solo French horn and flute over shimmering strings and harp, swelling to one radiant full-orchestra climax with soft timpani, then ends on a long resolved major chord that rings out. Production: warm concert-hall reverb.
